turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hello there! How's your day treating you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My son's nine and he's borrowed my old camera. How do I explain composition to a kid?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Try the noughts and crosses game. Imagine that grid over the picture and put the interesting thing where two lines cross, not right in the middle.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ooh, he'd like that. He loves noughts and crosses.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You can even turn the grid on in the camera settings, so he sees it on screen.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What else, without turning it into a lesson?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Give him little missions. Find something red, take a photo from as low as a mouse, take one from on top of a chair.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He's going to lie on the floor of the supermarket, isn't he.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Quite possibly. But he'll learn more from that than from any rule. Look through his photos together after and ask which one he likes most and why.
